LLM-Based Applications基于 LLM 的应用

— 原书第 61 页 —

As of early 2025, only a few companies offer large multimodal models that can understand and generate text, images, and other media, like sound and video. For brevity, we will call these AI models. The most well-known examples are the GPT models created by OpenAI, but a few other popular examples are the Gemini models created by Google, the Claude Sonnet and Haiku models created by Anthropic, and the Llama models created by Meta.

截至 2025 年初，只有少数几家公司提供能理解并生成文本、图像以及声音、视频等其他媒体的大型多模态模型。为简便起见，我们称这些为 AI 模型。最著名的例子是 OpenAI 创建的 GPT 模型，其他一些流行例子包括 Google 创建的 Gemini 模型、Anthropic 创建的 Claude Sonnet 和 Haiku 模型，以及 Meta 创建的 Llama 模型。

In many cases, these companies partner with other companies to offer these models as a cloud service. For example, OpenAI has a partnership with Microsoft, which provides the infrastructure to host OpenAI's models in cloud services that can be accessed via APIs. Other companies, like Meta, provide a model snapshot, a large binary file containing the weights of a pretrained model, which users can install in their own infrastructure. This infrastructure can be "bare metal," meaning physical machines the companies own, or cloud infrastructure they purchase from other providers.

在许多情况下，这些公司与其他公司合作，把这些模型作为云服务提供。例如 OpenAI 与微软合作，微软提供基础设施把 OpenAI 的模型托管在云服务中，可通过 API 访问。另一些公司如 Meta 则提供模型快照——一个包含预训练模型权重的大型二进制文件，用户可安装在自己的基础设施上。这种基础设施可以是“裸金属”（即公司自有的物理机器），也可以是从其他提供商购买的云基础设施。

Model-building companies also offer user-facing applications. In many cases, the name of the model and the name of the user-facing application are the same or very similar, making it easy to confuse the two. For example, the Google Gemini application uses the Google Gemini model, and the Claude application uses the Anthropic Claude Sonnet and Haiku models. OpenAI's names are slightly different: its user-facing application, ChatGPT, allows users to interact with the GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini models.

构建模型的公司也提供面向用户的应用。在很多情况下，模型名和面向用户的应用名相同或非常相似，容易混淆。例如 Google Gemini 应用使用 Google Gemini 模型，Claude 应用使用 Anthropic Claude Sonnet 和 Haiku 模型。OpenAI 的命名略有不同：其面向用户的应用 ChatGPT 允许用户与 GPT-4o 和 GPT-4o-mini 模型交互。

— 原书第 62 页 —

These applications can have different levels of sophistication. The simplest type of application is a chat-like web interface that allows users to send prompts directly to the model and returns the response. These days, most of the applications provided by large companies are more sophisticated than that. Instead of simply passing prompts directly, they add several layers of their own instructions to the user input, keep track of what the user asked earlier in that conversation (and sometimes in previous sessions), modify the user-submitted prompt to increase the chance of getting a better response, and ensure that their answers are safe and polite.

这些应用的复杂程度各不相同。最简单的类型是类似聊天的 Web 界面，允许用户直接向模型发送提示并返回回复。如今，大公司提供的大多数应用都比这更复杂。它们不是简单地把提示直接传递，而是在用户输入之上加几层自己的指令，跟踪用户在该对话中（有时还有之前会话中）问过什么，修改用户提交的提示以提高获得更好回复的概率，并确保回答安全、礼貌。

Given these additional prompts and safeguards, users get different answers when interacting with models through the API and through the default web application. For example, when a user is interacting with ChatGPT on the web through chatgpt.com, they are likely to get different answers than if they were to submit the same prompt directly to the model using an API. The answer from ChatGPT may use data from previous chats and will add some additional safeguards and instructions to the user-provided prompt. For example, when you ask a question using ChatGPT's website, it now usually finishes the response with a question inviting the user to continue the conversation, like "Would you like to explore more?" If you use the model directly from the API, it will not include this conversational phrase.

由于这些额外的提示和安全措施，用户通过 API 和通过默认 Web 应用与模型交互时会得到不同的答案。例如，用户通过 chatgpt.com 在网页上与 ChatGPT 交互时，得到的答案很可能与直接用 API 向模型提交同一提示不同。ChatGPT 的回答可能使用之前聊天的数据，并在用户提供的提示上加一些额外的安全措施和指令。例如，你用 ChatGPT 网站提问时，它现在通常会在回复末尾加一句邀请用户继续对话的话，比如“你想进一步探索吗？”如果你直接从 API 使用模型，就不会包含这句对话用语。

Companies don't have to develop and train an AI model in order to create an application that uses AI. They can license and integrate existing models such as Gemini, Claude, or GPT-4o into their user-facing applications. Since 2023, a large proportion of repositories in GitHub have been importing code that allows use of the OpenAI APIs, indicating that many developers are using the GPT cloud services to add AI features to their own applications, as shown in Figure 3-1.

公司不必为了创建使用 AI 的应用而去开发和训练 AI 模型。它们可以授权并集成现有模型（如 Gemini、Claude 或 GPT-4o）到面向用户的应用中。自 2023 年以来，GitHub 上很大比例的仓库都在导入允许使用 OpenAI API 的代码，表明许多开发者正在使用 GPT 云服务为自己的应用添加 AI 功能，如图 3-1 所示。

This chapter discusses the operational considerations for using AI models in user-facing applications.

本章讨论在面向用户的应用中使用 AI 模型的运维考量。

— 原书第 63 页 —

Using AI Models in Applications在应用中使用 AI 模型

Many application tasks that were formerly assisted by automation and machine learning are now using AI models. The difference between implementing automation yourself and using a foundation model is subtle but consequential, especially for LLMOps.

许多过去由自动化和机器学习辅助的应用任务，现在改用 AI 模型。自己实现自动化与使用基础模型之间的差异微妙但影响深远，对 LLMOps 尤其如此。

— 原书第 64 页 —

Before machine learning and foundation models, if you wanted to automate a task, you would need to code it yourself, programming all the possible inputs and corresponding outputs for the application. In the last decade, a lot of this automation code could be replaced by training a model using machine learning. When a new input was submitted, the ML model would generate an appropriate output, even if that input was not explicitly programmed or previously seen by the model.

在机器学习和基础模型出现之前，如果你想自动化一个任务，就得自己写代码，为应用编程所有可能的输入和对应输出。过去十年，很多这种自动化代码可以通过训练一个机器学习模型来替代。当提交新输入时，ML 模型会生成合适的输出，即使该输入没有被显式编程或模型之前没见过。

Here are some examples of popular consumer-facing applications that incorporate third-party foundation models:

以下是一些流行的、集成了第三方基础模型的面向消费者应用：

  • BeMyEyes. This OpenAI application helps people who are blind or have low vision to navigate the world better by using their phones. They can point their phone cameras at things and hear rich descriptions. They can use the app to count money, to identify products in the supermarket, and to assist with using automated teller machines. They can even point the app at their computer screens to get technical support.BeMyEyes。这个 OpenAI 应用帮助盲人和低视力人士通过手机更好地认识世界。他们可以把手机摄像头对准物体，听到丰富的描述。他们可以用这个应用数钱、在超市识别商品、协助使用自动取款机。甚至可以把应用对准电脑屏幕来获得技术支持。
  • Duolingo. This foreign language–learning application uses LLMs to create lessons faster and with more variety. The models are used to generate more versions of dialogues that adhere to difficulty standards, making lessons less repetitive and more enjoyable.Duolingo。这个外语学习应用使用 LLM 更快、更多样地创建课程。模型被用来生成更多符合难度标准的对话版本，让课程不那么重复、更有趣。
  • Khan Academy. This educational website is used by hundreds of millions of people to learn academic subjects, mainly those taught in grades K–12. Khan Academy offers Khanmigo (a portmanteau of Khan and amigo, Spanish and Portuguese for "friend"), which serves as a study buddy and personal tutor. Students can ask Khanmigo questions about careers and why the lesson they're taking is useful for their lives (a favorite question among teenagers: "Ugh, why do I have to learn this?"). Khanmigo can also generate quizzes to assess learning, provide feedback on the student's writing and answers, and generally help a student without providing the answers directly.Khan Academy。这个教育网站被数亿人用来学习学科，主要是 K-12 年级的内容。Khan Academy 提供 Khanmigo（Khan 与 amigo 的合成词，amigo 在西班牙语和葡萄牙语中意为“朋友”），充当学习伙伴和私人导师。学生可以问 Khanmigo 关于职业的问题，以及为什么正在学的课程对生活有用（青少年最爱问的问题：“唉，我为什么要学这个？”）。Khanmigo 还能生成测验来评估学习，对学生的写作和答案提供反馈，总体上帮助学生而不直接给出答案。
  • Microsoft Copilot. The Copilot stack accounts for perhaps the widest deployment of AI to date. Available in several popular Microsoft products, including Office, Windows, and Bing, the Copilot products help users accomplish common tasks quicker. For example, you can open Word and ask Copilot to "write a letter to Bank of America asking to close my checking account." A letter automatically populates with the appropriate language, and you just need to fill in a few blanks. Another frequently used example is converting Word documents to PowerPoint presentations and vice versa.Microsoft Copilot。Copilot 技术栈可能是迄今为止 AI 最广泛的部署。它出现在 Office、Windows、Bing 等多个微软热门产品中，帮助用户更快完成常见任务。例如，你可以打开 Word，让 Copilot“写一封信给美国银行要求关闭我的支票账户”。信件会自动填上合适的措辞，你只需填几个空。另一个常用例子是把 Word 文档转换为 PowerPoint 演示文稿，反之亦然。
— 原书第 65 页 —

Build Versus Buy. When using an AI model in your application, one of the main decisions is whether to build your own model from scratch, start from a model and improve it through fine-tuning and/or prompt engineering, or simply use an existing model out of the box. The considerations for this decision are covered in Chapter 1. This chapter assumes that the decision has already been made and you already have one or more models ready to use in your application.

自建 vs 采购。在应用中使用 AI 模型时，主要决策之一是：从零构建自己的模型，从某个模型出发通过微调和/或提示工程改进，还是直接开箱使用现有模型。这一决策的考量在第 1 章已覆盖。本章假设决策已做出，你已有一个或多个模型可在应用中使用。

Infrastructure Applications基础设施类应用

While the first wave of LLM applications was mostly focused on user-facing tools for tasks like writing and summarization, the current wave of LLM-based applications is largely focused on infrastructure applications that make LLMs faster, more programmable, and more modular. They redefine what an LLM is and how it can be used. LLM applications are no longer limited to chatbots: they have become a new layer of code in software applications. (This is what we referred to as Software 3.0 in Chapter 2.) Let's look at some of these uses, one by one.

第一波 LLM 应用主要面向写作、摘要等任务的用户工具，而当前这波基于 LLM 的应用则主要聚焦于基础设施类应用，让 LLM 更快、更可编程、更模块化。它们重新定义了 LLM 是什么以及如何使用。LLM 应用不再局限于聊天机器人：它们已成为软件应用中新的一层代码。（这就是第 2 章所说的 Software 3.0。）我们逐一看看这些用途。

Agentic Workflows智能体工作流

A single prompt can take you far. But for anything beyond a surface-level task, you need more than one-shot queries. You need memory. You need planning. You need tools. And eventually, you need agents that can act—not just complete a prompt but choose what to do next. This is where the shift from language models to agentic systems comes in.

单个提示能走很远。但对于表面任务之外的任何事，你需要的不只是一次性查询。你需要记忆。需要规划。需要工具。最终你需要能行动的智能体——不只是完成提示，而是选择下一步做什么。这就是从语言模型向智能体系统转变的切入点。

At its core, an agent is just a loop. It observes, decides, and acts—over and over. Those acts might be to read an instruction, check its current state, fetch a resource, call a tool, or break a task into smaller ones. Each of those actions requires reasoning, and each decision affects what happens next. In an agentic system, the model is no longer passive. It's running code, managing steps, and adapting as it goes.

核心上，智能体就是一个循环。它观察、决策、行动——周而复始。这些行动可能是读取指令、检查当前状态、获取资源、调用工具，或把任务拆成更小的子任务。每个行动都需要推理，每个决策都影响接下来发生什么。在智能体系统中，模型不再被动。它在运行代码、管理步骤、随进展调整。

This approach unlocks more complex workflows. Instead of a user stitching together model calls by hand, an agent handles the logic. It can retry failures, store intermediate state, track objectives, and even call other agents. This isn't prompt engineering anymore—it's system design.

这种方法解锁了更复杂的工作流。不再由用户手工拼接模型调用，而是由智能体处理逻辑。它可以重试失败、存储中间状态、跟踪目标，甚至调用其他智能体。这不再是提示工程——这是系统设计。

Not all agents operate the same way. Some follow a fixed plan; others adapt in real time. Some agents think once, act once, and stop. Others operate in loops, revisiting goals and shifting strategy as needed. Understanding these differences helps in designing systems that are robust, interpretable, and efficient. Major types of agents include:

并非所有智能体都以同样方式运作。有的遵循固定计划；有的实时适应。有的智能体思考一次、行动一次就停止。有的在循环中运作，反复回顾目标、按需调整策略。理解这些差异有助于设计健壮、可解释、高效的系统。智能体的主要类型包括：

— 原书第 66 页 —
  • Single-step agents. The simplest form of an agent is little more than a wrapped prompt. It takes an input, does some local reasoning, returns an output, and exits. There's no memory, no iteration, no feedback loop. These are useful when the task is bounded, like generating a SQL query, converting a paragraph to a tweet, or answering a direct question. But single-step agents are brittle. They assume everything is known up front. They can't handle surprises or partial failures. You'll quickly outgrow them when tasks involve multiple actions or require state tracking.单步智能体。最简单的智能体形式不过是包装了一层的提示。它接收输入、做些本地推理、返回输出然后退出。没有记忆、没有迭代、没有反馈循环。当任务有边界时它们很有用，比如生成 SQL 查询、把一段文字转成推文，或回答直接的问题。但单步智能体很脆弱。它们假设一切事先已知，无法处理意外或部分失败。当任务涉及多个行动或需要状态跟踪时，你很快就会不够用。
  • Chain-of-thought agents. Here, the agent reasons step-by-step—often in the same prompt. Instead of jumping straight to the answer, it explains its logic first. This internal decomposition improves reasoning and often leads to better performance on multi-hop problems. However, the limitation is clear: it's still all happening within a single model call. There's no memory of what was done before. If the chain is too long or the context window too short, the agent breaks.思维链智能体。这里智能体逐步推理——通常在同一个提示内。它不是直接跳到答案，而是先解释自己的逻辑。这种内部分解改善了推理，往往在多跳问题上表现更好。但局限也很明显：一切仍在单次模型调用内发生。它不记得之前做过什么。如果链条太长或上下文窗口太短，智能体就会崩。
  • Plan-and-act agents. This is where things get more interesting. These agents first generate a high-level plan, then execute it step-by-step. For example, if you tasked a plan-and-ask agent with writing a blog post, it would start by drafting an outline. Then it would write each section separately, check for coherence, and edit the result. The planning and acting can happen in the same model or across separate agents. This structure introduces what has been done, what's left, and where things went wrong. It also allows for retries and self-correction. If a step fails, the agent can replan or fall back to an alternative.规划-执行智能体。事情在这里变得更有意思。这些智能体先生成高层计划，再逐步执行。例如，如果你让一个规划-询问智能体写博客，它会先起草大纲，然后分别写每一节、检查连贯性、编辑结果。规划和执行可以在同一模型中进行，也可以跨不同智能体。这种结构引入了已完成什么、还剩什么、哪里出了问题。它还允许重试和自我纠正。如果某步失败，智能体可以重新规划或回退到备选方案。
  • Reflective or self-improving agents. These agents don't just act—they reflect on their performance. After completing a task, they might score their own output, compare it with a ground truth, or even consult another model to improve their reasoning. This creates a feedback loop where the agent learns from its past actions—not in the ML training sense but in the runtime sense. Reflection is costly but powerful. It adds robustness, especially in open-ended domains where correctness is hard to define in advance.反思或自我改进智能体。这些智能体不只是行动——它们还反思自己的表现。完成任务后，它们可能给自己的输出打分、与标准答案比较，甚至请教另一个模型来改进推理。这创造了一个反馈循环，智能体从过去的行动中学习——不是 ML 训练意义上的，而是运行时意义上的。反思成本高但强大。它增加了鲁棒性，尤其在正确性难以预先定义的开放式领域。
  • Recursive decomposition agents. In this pattern, an agent tackles a task by recursively breaking it down. It might see a top-level goal, decide it's too big, and generate subtasks. It then becomes a manager—delegating each subtask to a new instance of itself or to other specialized agents. This pattern is used in systems like AutoGPT and BabyAGI. It allows for dynamic depth: tasks get decomposed until they're small enough to solve directly. The challenge is keeping the recursion from spiraling out of control, especially in the absence of tight constraints or time limits.递归分解智能体。在这种模式中，智能体通过递归拆解来处理任务。它可能看到一个顶层目标，判断太大，然后生成子任务。它于是变成管理者——把每个子任务委托给自己的新实例或其他专业智能体。这种模式用于 AutoGPT、BabyAGI 等系统。它允许动态深度：任务被拆解直到小到可以直接解决。挑战在于防止递归失控，尤其是在没有严格约束或时限时。
— 原书第 67 页 —
  • Multi-agent collaborators. Rather than using recursion, some systems distribute responsibility: one agent writes, another edits. One gathers data, another analyzes it. These agents have defined roles, often with isolated tools and memories. Communication happens through shared messages or task queues. This is effective when tasks are parallelizable or when each agent has domain-specific expertise. It also forces clear interfaces: each agent must expose how to talk to it and what kind of input it expects.多智能体协作者。有些系统不用递归，而是分配职责：一个智能体写，另一个编辑；一个收集数据，另一个分析。这些智能体有明确定义的角色，通常有隔离的工具和记忆。通信通过共享消息或任务队列进行。当任务可并行化或每个智能体有领域专业知识时，这很有效。它还迫使接口清晰：每个智能体必须暴露如何与它对话以及它期望什么输入。

Each of these patterns serves a different purpose. Some are simple, designed for speed. Others are more expressive, built for complexity. As models improve and infrastructure grows, we'll see these workflows combine—agents that reflect and recurse in combination with systems that plan, act, and then hand off to a team. As these systems scale, coordination becomes the challenge. One agent might specialize in math. Another might handle API queries. A third might focus on summarization. Instead of building a single monolithic agent that does everything, it makes more sense to compose smaller, focused agents that work together. This is where multi-agent systems enter. A multi-agent system isn't just a collection of bots. It's an architecture in which each agent operates semi-independently, often with its own tools, memory, and goals. The agents talk, delegate, and collaborate. For instance, one agent might take a user request and break it into subgoals. Another might execute a subtask and pass the result back. Over time, agents can even evolve internal protocols—figuring out how best to share information or resolve conflicts.

这些模式各有用途。有的简单，为速度设计；有的表达力更强，为复杂度构建。随着模型改进和基础设施增长，我们会看到这些工作流组合起来——反思和递归的智能体与规划、执行然后移交团队的系统结合。随着这些系统扩缩，协调成为挑战。一个智能体可能专攻数学，另一个处理 API 查询，第三个专注摘要。与其构建一个包揽一切的巨石智能体，不如组合更小、更专注的智能体协同工作。这就是多智能体系统登场的地方。多智能体系统不只是一堆机器人，而是一种架构：每个智能体半独立运作，通常有自己的工具、记忆和目标。智能体之间对话、委托、协作。例如，一个智能体接收用户请求并拆成子目标，另一个执行子任务并把结果传回。久而久之，智能体甚至能演化出内部协议——摸索出共享信息或解决冲突的最佳方式。

Designing these workflows is not trivial. The more agents you add, the more coordination overhead you introduce. You have to define roles, communication boundaries, and fallback plans. You need logging, observability, and memory management. You also need clarity around failure; for example, what happens when one agent goes silent or another returns an error?

设计这些工作流并非易事。加入的智能体越多，协调开销越大。你必须定义角色、通信边界和回退计划。你需要日志、可观测性和记忆管理。你还需要对失败有清晰认识；例如，一个智能体沉默或另一个返回错误时会怎样？

That's why agentic design is not just about the model—it requires control flow. What decisions should happen inside the model versus outside of it? What should be handled by logic, and what should be learned? These are architectural questions, not just engineering ones.

这就是为什么智能体设计不只是关于模型——它需要控制流。哪些决策应在模型内做、哪些在模型外？哪些由逻辑处理、哪些应被学习？这些是架构问题，不只是工程问题。

As of now, we're still early in this transition. The industry is moving from LLMs as isolated prompt responders toward full-blown systems that can think in steps, delegate across agents, and operate over time. To make this possible, it needs shared protocols like MCP and A2A, which we discuss next. These protocols provide conventions that let agents talk, reason, and act as a team.

目前我们仍处于这一转变的早期。行业正从作为孤立提示响应者的 LLM，走向能分步思考、跨智能体委托、长期运作的完整系统。要实现这一点，需要 MCP 和 A2A 这样的共享协议，我们接下来讨论。这些协议提供约定，让智能体作为团队对话、推理和行动。
